title: TripLOG expense summary concepts
request: 이 부분디자인톤안맞는데 디자인톤 맞게 뛰어난 Ui,UX로 목업 만든후 개선
status: Three independent concepts generated; awaiting user visual selection before implementation.

observations: Current light-blue box places the total and per-person amount in similarly sized columns.
The surrounding expense UI uses yellow and pale-blue accents with crisp dark borders.
The new summary should keep total spending first, average second, and record count/supporting scope text third.
evidence.scope: Single summary component, with adjacent page context captured. No full accessibility audit was performed.

generationPolicy: Independent built-in T2I calls; no screenshot or previous generated image supplied to any generation. User AGENTS.md T2I instruction takes precedence over generic attach-reference skill instructions.

outputs.prompt:
Create a production-quality responsive expense-summary UI concept for the existing TripLOG Korean travel planner. Use one concept shown at two responsive sizes on a clean white 1440 × 680 presentation canvas: a desktop component 912 CSS px wide near the top, and its mobile adaptation 358 CSS px wide below. These are two sizes of the same design, not different options. Keep realistic UI scale and readable Korean typography; do not stretch either rendering.

The component helps travelers read their cumulative spending first, then the per-person average and number of recorded expenses. Render this exact content: “여행 경비”, “486,000원”, “1인 평균”, “243,000원”, “기록한 지출 14건”, and the small supporting line “사전구매·환불 포함 · 누적 금액”. The data represents actual spending, not a budget target.

Direction: a confident total-first summary. Give total spending a bold yellow emphasis and let the supporting facts feel lighter and neatly grouped. Explore a compact composition with a clear visual reading order and purposeful whitespace.

Match TripLOG’s existing visual language: white surface, near-black #0b1020 ink and crisp outlines, sunny yellow #fff05a, pale blue #bce6fb as a restrained supporting accent, rounded corners, minimal hard offset shadow, Pretendard-style Korean sans-serif, and clean line icons. Use approximately 14–16 CSS px labels, a 30–34 px primary amount and a 22–24 px secondary amount; preserve readable sizes on mobile. Use icons only where they help identify the information.

Design only this focused summary. No additional metrics, charts, budget progress, controls, navigation, device frames, browser chrome, decorative scenery, or explanatory design-board text. Keep the total visibly more prominent than the average. Avoid nested cards and excessive empty space. Current date is 2026-10-13; no dates need to appear in this component.
